goal: Replace the enum keyword with ML-style sum type syntax (type SchoolPerson = | Teacher | Student(name: string)), keeping today's semantics

extra_axes.name: language
extra_axes.why: a keyword change costs and gains only in how code reads and what users and models expect
extra_axes.ruling_why: every deciding claim is about TypeScript habits, D2 and readability

claims.text: D2: where Narra's meaning differs from TypeScript's, Narra uses different syntax or an error with a fix; the same text never means two things. SPEC section 2 already lists `enum` as a known difference (TS: named numbers or strings; Narra: variants with fields).

TypeScript enum text mostly keeps its meaning in Narra: `enum Color { Red, Green }` compiles as fieldless constructors, read as Color.Red after the qualified-constructor debate. `Red = 1` is a parse error ('expected a name, found "="') with no fix.

In TypeScript, `type Shape = Circle | Square` is a union of existing types Circle and Square. Under the proposal, the same text would declare two new constructors named Circle and Square. Today it is a parse error.

evidence.source: narra run evidence/tsunion.nra; TS handbook (union types)

claims.text: `type A = B` already means an alias (SPEC section 3) and `distinct type A = B` a new nominal type. The proposal makes `type` declare a nominal sum type when the right side starts with `|`.

Prior art: Rust, Swift, Haxe and Kotlin (enum class / sealed) use `enum` for sums with payloads. OCaml, F#, Haskell, Elm, Gleam and ReScript use `type ... = | A | B`. ReScript targets JS users with ML syntax throughout, not TS syntax.
68 enum declarations across selfhost and compiler/testdata; `enum` is parsed at parser.go:196/402 and in selfhost/src/parser.nra. Also `@repr(u8) enum` (SPEC section 12) and `derives` refer to enums.
The previous debate settled qualified access, SchoolPerson.Teacher, which is exactly how TypeScript reads enum members.
Declare sum types as `type SchoolPerson = | Teacher | Director | Student(name: string)` and drop the `enum` keyword. Semantics stay the same.
claims.ruling_why: J3: the TypeScript reading of the same text is a union of existing types, so this reuses TS syntax with a different meaning, which D2 forbids; enum's mismatch (P2) is the smaller one

claims.text: By D2's own rule `enum` is the wrong word: TS enums are named constants, Narra enums are tagged unions, and SPEC already has to call this out.
claims.ruling_why: J2: for every TS enum that Narra accepts, the meaning carries over (fieldless members, Color.Red access); the payload form is new syntax with no TS meaning, so no text means two things. Rust and Swift (J5) took the same path

claims.text: One declaration word (`type`) for aliases, distinct types and sums reads uniformly.
claims.ruling_why: J4: `type` would then mean alias or new nominal type depending on the first token of the right side; struct, enum and trait each have their own keyword today, and sum types fit that pattern

claims.text: TypeScript users and models will write `type Shape = Circle | Square` meaning a union of their structs, and get new constructors that shadow or clash with those struct names instead.
68 declarations, two parsers, SPEC, @repr and derives text change. Mechanical, but it lands in the same selfhost files as the constructor migration.
Keep `enum`. Fix the one TS-habit gap J2 found: `Red = 1` should get an error whose fix points to @repr and Enum.fromInt.
